agenda_items.title: Chair's Verbal Update
agenda_items.minutes:
April Programs at OPL
Chair Luloff highlighted upcoming celebrations of National Canadian Film Day featuring Canadian films and filmmakers in partnership with REEL Canada, a panel event at the Ruth E. Dickinson branch called “The Magic of the Short Story,” featuring contributors to “A Capital Mystery,” and noted that information about more spring programming is available on the OPL website.
Sunnyside 75th Anniversary
Chair Luloff thanked Board members, including Vice-Chair Kathy Fisher, Jessica Bradley, Alison Crawford, Rawlson King, and Harvey Slack, as well as Councillor Shawn Menard and MP Yasir Naqvi, for joining him and staff at the Sunnyside branch’s recent 75th anniversary celebration. Guests shared heartfelt reflections about the library’s lasting impact, describing Sunnyside as an intergenerational gathering place that has shaped lives for decades. The Chair further extended gratitude to all clients and staff for making the milestone event a true tribute to everything libraries bring to their communities.
MOTION OPL 20260414/1
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the Chair’s verbal update for information.
Results: Received

agenda_items.title: Chief Executive Officer / Chief Librarian’s Report
agenda_items.minutes:
One eRead Canada 2026
Sonia Bebbington, Chief Executive Officer/Chief Librarian (CEO/CL) highlighted One eRead/Un Livrel Canada, Canada’s national digital book club, now underway and featuring Eric Chacour’s “What I Know About You.” The program brings readers and libraries together across the country to promote e-reading and to highlight the importance of sustainable licensing for eBooks in public libraries, and features two author events. Details are available on the OPL website.
Volunteer Month
Ms. Bebbington recognized the vital role of volunteers for Volunteer Month and National Volunteer Week, including the more than 400 volunteers who contributed nearly 9,700 hours of service in 2025, including many teens involved in branch Teen Advisory Groups such as those who recently helped celebrate Sunnyside’s 75th anniversary. She particularly noted the contributions of the Friends of the Ottawa Public Library Association (FOPLA) volunteers and those of OPL Board members. A small token of appreciation from a local business in Rawlson King’s ward was provided to each Board member. Ms. Bebbington also recognized Vice-Chair Fisher for her long-standing volunteer service with the Federation of Ontario Public Libraries and its Indigenous Working Group.
MOTION OPL 20260414/2
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the Chief Librarian/CEO’s report for information.
Results: Received

sub_agendas_items.title: Friends of the Ottawa Public Library Association
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Sonia Bebbington, CEO/CL, introduced Alexandra Yarrow, Program Manager, Board and Strategic Services and staff FOPLA lead, and Kathleen O’Connell Renaud, President, Friends of the Ottawa Public Library Association (FOPLA). Ms. O’Connell Renaud provided a presentation about FOPLA, including an overview of the organization, its stores/boutiques, its bursaries and scholarships, a summary of recent achievements, and the impact of FOPLA’s donation to OPL in the community. She provided a brief overview of the investment fund, risk management, and website refresh. Ms. Yarrow listed FOPLA’s 2025 gift in action which funds many branch activities. (Held on file with the Chief Executive Officer/Chief Librarian).
Ms. O’Connell Renaud announced that the 2026 FOPLA donation to OPL is $232,800 and thanked the Board and staff for their continued support of FOPLA.
Chair Luloff expressed his deep gratitude to FOPLA for the generous annual donation and ongoing support of the OPL. He highlighted how dedicated and welcoming the FOPLA volunteers are, noting his own positive interactions at various branches and how evident it is that volunteers genuinely love their work. He also thanked OPL staff for consistently supporting FOPLA’s in-branch book sales. He emphasized the strong, collaborative relationship between FOPLA and OPL, recognizing FOPLA as leaders both within the community and among Friends organizations more broadly.
Harvey A. Slack congratulated Ms. O’Connell Renaud for FOPLA’s meaningful contributions, and mentioned his own volunteer contributions at the Rockcliffe Park Friends Book Sale, including donating several cases of books.
In closing, Chair Luloff mentioned that the next FOPLA’s Mammoth Book Sale will take place on April 25th at 100 Tallwood.
There being no further discussion, the presentation was RECEIVED as presented.
MOTION OPL 20260414/3
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the presentation for information.
Results: Received

sub_agendas_items.title: Accessibility Roadmap for Client Service Delivery
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Sonia Bebbington, CEO/CL introduced Sarah Macintyre, Division Manager, Client Services, Robin Gallagher, Program Manager, Client Experience and Community Development, and Sarah Reive, Library Planning Consultant, Access and User Experience who delivered a presentation (held on file with the Chief Executive Officer/Chief Librarian) updating the Board on the purpose of the Accessibility Roadmap. The following is a summary of the information presented:
Vice-Chair Kathy Fisher asked whether staff could share a copy of the presentation with the Board and Ms. Bebbington confirmed in the affirmative. Following the meeting, staff shared a memo and a copy of the presentation with the Board on April 27, 2026 and these items were added to the May 12 meeting package as Information Previously Distributed.
In response to a question from Vice-Chair Fisher seeking clarification about the term “barrier theme analysis,” Ms. Reive explained that this process involves gathering input from community members about the barriers they experience, grouping those barriers into themes, and then assessing them based on two factors: how important the issue is to the community; and, how difficult it would be to implement solutions with available resources. This process helps prioritize which accessibility barriers should be addressed first.
Alison Crawford inquired about the accessibility-related feedback staff have been receiving from community members. Ms. Gallagher outlined key themes:
In response to a question from Ms. Crawford about whether OPL has collaborated with local accessibility organizations, Ms. Bebbington noted long-standing collaboration with groups like the Centre for Equitable Library Access to loan accessible formats and devices, as well as ongoing and future potential collaborations with the Abilities Centre and the City of Ottawa’s Accessibility Advisory Committee. Ms. Macintyre further noted collaboration with the Canadian National Institute for the Blind (CNIB) and others, adding that other public libraries doing accessibility work tend to share knowledge openly, and connecting with other library systems has been especially helpful for understanding best practices in this area.
Ms. Crawford pointed out that Centennial School, near the Central branch at Ādisōke, serves students with a wide range of disabilities, and urged staff to connect with staff there. Ms. Macintyre thanked Ms. Crawford for this connection.
Harvey A. Slack supported Ms. Crawford’s point regarding local community connections and further suggested connecting with Bruyère Health Saint-Vincent Hospital, The Good Companions, Ottawa Community Housing, and other nearby organizations around the Central branch, noting that the area has many valuable community resources.
Catherine Kitts thanked the team for their work. She noted that she recently attended the Public Library Association (PLA) Conference in Minneapolis, Minnesota and asked whether the Ottawa Public Library has an adaptive book collection. Ms. Macintyre asked for clarification about this format, noting that OPL offers materials such as phonics-supportive books, Wonder Books with audio, and braille books. Ms. Kitts provided additional details regarding adaptive books, and Ms. Macintyre noted that staff will explore this format further.
Chair Luloff briefly left the meeting at 5:43pm and returned at 5:45pm.
There being no further discussion, the presentation was RECEIVED as presented.
MOTION OPL 20260414/4
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the presentation for information.
Results: Received
